# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 91 (Bu-Vb Pc91)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc91  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 91  
**Title (English, from literature):** Making an oversize rainy-season robe  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vassikasāṭikā-sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 91) is a Vinaya rule establishing that a monk who makes a rainy-season robe (*vassikasāṭikā*) exceeding the permitted standard measurements must cut it down to size and confess an expiation offense (*pācittiya*). In modern scholarship, Valentina Stache-Rosen highlights that while rules 89 and 90 of the *Upāliparipṛcchāsūtra* treat upper and lower robes, Pācittiya 91 in the Pali tradition specifically concerns the rainy-season robe [Stache-Rosen 1984]. Ute Hüsken notes that this rule applies exclusively to monks, pointing to a discrepancy in the commentary *Samantapāsādikā* regarding the classification of rainy-season robe regulations as inapplicable to nuns while simultaneously discussing monastic boundary determinations (*sīmā*) [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
